properties.name: loop_status stops re-reading a hundred megabytes
properties.rationale:
⭐⭐ THE RULE THAT SHIPPED IS THE SECOND ONE TRIED, AND THE FIRST ONE'S FAILURE IS THE MORE USEFUL RECORD. The first attempt at ② refused to track anything under the OS temp directory, reasoning that scratch is not a SHARED record — which is what `req:a-seat-learns-the-record-moved-before-it-writes` exists for. FIFTEEN TESTS IN `the_record_moved_and_the_session_is_told` FAILED AND EVERY ONE WAS RIGHT: a hermetic test puts a genuine shared record in a temp dir, and so does a CI workspace and so does a container. One of them is named "the case the whole thing exists for — your brother pushed, you pulled". The rule fit every path on one machine and would have silenced the feature for everyone whose workspace sits under /tmp. The defect was never WHERE records live; it is that the list only grows. So the bound is on COUNT and assumes nothing about anybody's filesystem — and it is SLOWER than the wrong rule (23.6s rather than 14.3s) because it keeps six targets rather than two. That is the correct trade.

⭐⭐ AND CAUSE ① SHIPPED PAST TEN PASSING TESTS, because every one ran on an in-memory graph small enough that 483 scans were instant. Correctness was verified and cost was never measured once. AGENTS.md already says it — "compiling is not the finish line, and neither is a green unit test" — and what caught this was not a gate but a user asking for something else. A rollup that walks the graph needs a measurement at real scale before it merges.

🛑 A THIRD ERROR, RECORDED BECAUSE IT SHAPED THE WORK: the 40s was first attributed to cause ① on nothing but two similar numbers, and a fix was recommended on that basis. Scoping ① left `loop_status` unmoved; the cost was ②. Two numbers agreeing is not causation, and the attribution should have been measured before it was stated.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: `loop_status` measured 40.5s over the shared server on this graph (3,083 nodes / 13,188 edges) — the call `cap:loop-status` promises is ONE CHEAP CALL and every session is told to run. Two independent causes, both fixed. ① `invalidated_findings` asked `incoming()` of every Verification and TemporalFact, and each walks the whole edge set: 483 nodes x a full-graph scan, 39s, to return 1.2 KB saying nothing was claimed. The rollups now ask only about the rows they annotate (`invalidated_verifications`); the exhaustive form stays for the standalone tool. ② The list of synced records was unbounded — 16 targets totalling 102 MB, fourteen of them one-off probe dumps from past sessions, three belonging to another project, all re-read every time. A roll now opens the 6 most recently modified and reports the rest in `not_checked`. MEASURED AFTER: `loop_status` 23.6s, `sync_status` 28.3s -> 11.8s.
